subject: When performing multigroup analysis, are the factor scores standardized for each group?

messages.author: 9403604069d4685f
messages.subject: When performing multigroup analysis, are the factor scores standardized for each group?
parts:
Hello!

I have a data file containing the responses to a questionnaire over the course of 10 years. However, the data is not longitudinal, but cross-sectional (different people filled it out each year). I want to see if the measured construct is changing over time. When looking at the raw means, it appears that it does. However, I want to see if people are responding to the questionnaire in the same way across the years. In other words, I want to test for measurement invariance. For that purpose, I conducted a multiple group analysis in lavaan, with year being the group. Using the measurementInvariance function from semTools I found out that only configural invariance is established. Furthermore, I found out that reliability is changing over the years, with minimum being around .7 and maximum around .8.

However, my next question is: if there is no measurement invariance, how is the measured construct really changing over the years? For that purpose, I used the lavPredict function to obtain the factor scores and I have plotted them over the years. But, I am getting almost a flat line and I am afraid that the factor scores are standardized for each year (group) separately, therefore showing that the construct is not changing over the years.

Is this assumption correct? If it is, how would I go on about this problem? Is there another way to predict factor scores from a multiple group object where the scores are not standardized for each year separately?

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: When performing multigroup analysis, are the factor scores standardized for each group?
parts:
By default, the mean of a latent variable is zero (for identification purposes). If you want to look for change, you need to identify the mean in some other way. To do this, you fix the mean of the first latent variable to zero, then constrain intercepts (and loadings) of items across groups to be equal, and free the means of the latent variables of the other group(s).  

Perhaps post your code?

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: When performing multigroup analysis, are the factor scores standardized for each group?
parts:
You constrain across groups by giving the same label.

Something like:

LS =~ LS1 + c(lam2, lam2, lam2) * LS2 + 
          c(lam3, lam3, lam3) * LS3 +
          c(lam4, lam4, lam4) * LS4 +
          c(lam5, lam5, lam5) * LS5 +
          c(lam6, lam6, lam6) * LS6  

(There's also the measurementinvariance() function in semTools, see http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/multiplegroup6Dec2012.pdf ).

model.ls<-'

LS =~ LS1 + LS2 + LS3 + LS4 + LS5 + LS6
LS ~~ LS
LS1 ~~ LS5

LS4 ~ 1
LS5 ~ 1
LS6 ~ 1
LS ~ 1

messages.subject: Re: When performing multigroup analysis, are the factor scores standardized for each group?
parts: In some software, certain sets of parameters are constrained to be equal across groups by default, leading to the fulfillment of an important assumption called measurement invariance. Or the comparison of estimates would be meaningless.
